{
  "answers": [
    {
      "qid": 1,
      "question": "Does the paper report HIV sequences from patient samples?",
      "evidence": "“After RNA extraction, an in-house genotyping method and standard Sanger sequencing were used to amplify and sequence HIV-1 integrase genes, as described previously.” “Of 629 newly reported cases, the HIV-1 integrase genes of 601 cases were sequenced successfully.”",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "The Methods and Results on pages 1–2 report newly generated integrase sequences from clinical samples of individuals with HIV.",
      "answer": "Yes"
    },
    {
      "qid": 2,
      "question": "Does the paper report in vitro drug susceptibility data?",
      "evidence": "“We used the Stanford University HIV Drug Resistance Database (HIVDB Algorithm version 9.4.1) to examine mutations.” “Sequences with resistance levels classified as low, intermediate, and high were all regarded as resistant.”",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "Resistance classifications in Table 1 were inferred using HIVDB, not measured in phenotypic assays. The fold-change susceptibility statements in the discussion cite previous studies rather than new in vitro testing.",
      "answer": "No"
    },
    {
      "qid": 3,
      "question": "Were sequences from the paper made publicly available?",
      "evidence": "",
      "evidence_location": "not_found",
      "rationale": "The supplied article contains no sequence-repository accession numbers or deposition statement. Supplementary Table 1 is linked but is not included in the supplied file.",
      "answer": "No"
    },
    {
      "qid": 4,
      "question": "What are the GenBank accession numbers for sequenced HIV isolates?",
      "evidence": "",
      "evidence_location": "not_found",
      "rationale": "No GenBank or other sequence-repository accession numbers are provided in the supplied article.",
      "answer": "Not reported"
    },
    {
      "qid": 5,
      "question": "How many individuals had samples obtained for HIV sequencing?",
      "evidence": "“The current study recruited 629 ART-naïve individuals from Tianjin Second People’s Hospital between January 1, 2020, and April 1, 2023.” “Before initiating ART, 5 mL of blood was collected from the participants.” “Of 629 newly reported cases, the HIV-1 integrase genes of 601 cases were sequenced successfully.”",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "Samples were collected for sequencing from 629 individuals; sequencing succeeded for 601 of them.",
      "answer": "629"
    },
    {
      "qid": 6,
      "question": "From which countries were the sequenced samples obtained?",
      "evidence": "“This study evaluated the prevalence of INSTI-associated drug resistance among ART-naïve individuals infected with HIV-1 in Tianjin, China.” “The current study recruited 629 ART-naïve individuals from Tianjin Second People’s Hospital between January 1, 2020, and April 1, 2023.”",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "Participants were recruited and sampled in Tianjin, China.",
      "answer": "China"
    },
    {
      "qid": 7,
      "question": "From what years were the sequenced samples obtained?",
      "evidence": "“The current study recruited 629 ART-naïve individuals from Tianjin Second People’s Hospital between January 1, 2020, and April 1, 2023.” “Before initiating ART, 5 mL of blood was collected from the participants.”",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "Pretreatment sampling corresponds to recruitment during 2020–2023. Table 1 on page 2 also lists samples from each of these years.",
      "answer": "2020–2023"
    },
    {
      "qid": 8,
      "question": "Were samples cloned prior to sequencing?",
      "evidence": "“After RNA extraction, an in-house genotyping method and standard Sanger sequencing were used to amplify and sequence HIV-1 integrase genes, as described previously.” “We used the Stanford University HIV Drug Resistance Database (HIVDB Algorithm version 9.4.1) to examine mutations.”",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "The study does not report in vitro susceptibility testing, so the specified applicability rule requires Not applicable.",
      "answer": "Not applicable"
    },
    {
      "qid": 9,
      "question": "Which HIV genes were reported to have been sequenced?",
      "evidence": "“After RNA extraction, an in-house genotyping method and standard Sanger sequencing were used to amplify and sequence HIV-1 integrase genes, as described previously.” “Of 629 newly reported cases, the HIV-1 integrase genes of 601 cases were sequenced successfully.”",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "Only integrase is reported as a sequencing target in this study.",
      "answer": "IN"
    },
    {
      "qid": 10,
      "question": "What method was used for sequencing?",
      "evidence": "“After RNA extraction, an in-house genotyping method and standard Sanger sequencing were used to amplify and sequence HIV-1 integrase genes, as described previously.” “Of 629 newly reported cases, the HIV-1 integrase genes of 601 cases were sequenced successfully.”",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "The Methods explicitly identify standard Sanger sequencing.",
      "answer": "Sanger sequencing"
    },
    {
      "qid": 11,
      "question": "What type of samples were sequenced?",
      "evidence": "“Before initiating ART, 5 mL of blood was collected from the participants.” “After RNA extraction, an in-house genotyping method and standard Sanger sequencing were used to amplify and sequence HIV-1 integrase genes, as described previously.” “Of 629 newly reported cases, the HIV-1 integrase genes of 601 cases were sequenced successfully.”",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "Plasma is inferred under the specified rule for samples from newly reported cases before ART. The paper explicitly reports blood collection and RNA extraction but does not specify the blood fraction used.",
      "answer": "Plasma"
    },
    {
      "qid": 12,
      "question": "Were any sequences obtained from individuals with virological failure on a treatment regimen?",
      "evidence": "“The current study recruited 629 ART-naïve individuals from Tianjin Second People’s Hospital between January 1, 2020, and April 1, 2023.” “Before initiating ART, 5 mL of blood was collected from the participants.”",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "All participants were ART-naïve and were sampled before treatment, not during virological failure.",
      "answer": "No"
    },
    {
      "qid": 13,
      "question": "Were the patients in the study in a clinical trial?",
      "evidence": "“This study evaluated the prevalence of INSTI-associated drug resistance among ART-naïve individuals infected with HIV-1 in Tianjin, China.” “Baseline clinical and demographic data were obtained from the NFATP database, including sex, age, transmission route, CD4 count, and viral load.”",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "This is an observational pretreatment resistance survey. No treatment allocation, randomization, trial phase, or other evidence of clinical-trial participation is described.",
      "answer": "No"
    },
    {
      "qid": 14,
      "question": "Does the paper report HIV sequences from individuals who had previously received ARV drugs?",
      "evidence": "“The current study recruited 629 ART-naïve individuals from Tianjin Second People’s Hospital between January 1, 2020, and April 1, 2023.” “Before initiating ART, 5 mL of blood was collected from the participants.”",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "The sequenced population was exclusively ART-naïve, and eligibility required no prior antiviral treatment.",
      "answer": "No"
    },
    {
      "qid": 15,
      "question": "Which drug classes were received by individuals in the study before sample sequencing?",
      "evidence": "“The current study recruited 629 ART-naïve individuals from Tianjin Second People’s Hospital between January 1, 2020, and April 1, 2023.” “Before initiating ART, 5 mL of blood was collected from the participants.”",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "All sequenced participants were ART-naïve. Discussion of ARV classes used elsewhere in China or Tianjin does not establish exposure in this study population.",
      "answer": "None"
    },
    {
      "qid": 16,
      "question": "Which drugs were received by individuals in the study before sample sequencing?",
      "evidence": "“The current study recruited 629 ART-naïve individuals from Tianjin Second People’s Hospital between January 1, 2020, and April 1, 2023.” “Before initiating ART, 5 mL of blood was collected from the participants.”",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "Participants had no prior ARV treatment. Drugs named in the background and resistance interpretation are not reported as drugs received by the sequenced participants.",
      "answer": "None"
    }
  ]
}

{
  "answers": [
    {
      "qid": 1,
      "question": "Does the paper report HIV sequences from patient samples?",
      "evidence": "\"Genotypic resistance testing was carried out in the pol gene (reverse transcriptase and protease regions) as follows.\" \"A total of 391 participants were recruited, with sequencing successfully carried out in 379 individual participant samples, giving a genotyping success rate of 96.9%.\"",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "Methods section 2.5 and Results section 3.1 describe newly generated HIV sequences from clinical samples of study participants.",
      "answer": "Yes"
    },
    {
      "qid": 2,
      "question": "Does the paper report in vitro drug susceptibility data?",
      "evidence": "\"The predictive efficacies of each antiretroviral molecule were calculated according to the genotypic drug susceptibility score provided according to HIVdb algorithm (http://www.hivdb.stanford.edu, accessed on 24 May 2023).\" \"Regarding DTG efficacy, during the same study period, we reported a prevalence of 0% resistance to DTG in ART naïve patients, inferring 100% predictive efficacy of DTG [17].\"",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "Section 2.6 describes computational predictions based on genotypes and previously reported DTG resistance findings, not experimental phenotypic susceptibility measurements. No in vitro drug susceptibility assay is reported.",
      "answer": "No"
    },
    {
      "qid": 3,
      "question": "Were sequences from the paper made publicly available?",
      "evidence": "\"Sequence data are available on GenBank under the accession numbers GenBank MK702015-MK702057, MK867695-MK867757, and MK995397-MK995457.\" \"In total, 379 sequences were obtained from participants (62% female, mean age 36 ± 10 years).\"",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "The Data Availability Statement on page 11 explicitly identifies public GenBank deposits for study sequence data.",
      "answer": "Yes"
    },
    {
      "qid": 4,
      "question": "What are the GenBank accession numbers for sequenced HIV isolates?",
      "evidence": "\"Sequence data are available on GenBank under the accession numbers GenBank MK702015-MK702057, MK867695-MK867757, and MK995397-MK995457.\" \"In total, 379 sequences were obtained from participants (62% female, mean age 36 ± 10 years).\"",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "These are all three accession ranges listed in the Data Availability Statement on page 11.",
      "answer": "MK702015–MK702057; MK867695–MK867757; MK995397–MK995457"
    },
    {
      "qid": 5,
      "question": "How many individuals had samples obtained for HIV sequencing?",
      "evidence": "\"A total of 391 participants were recruited, with sequencing successfully carried out in 379 individual participant samples, giving a genotyping success rate of 96.9%.\" \"For each participant, 10 mL of venous blood was collected in an EDTA tube.\"",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "Sections 2.3 and 3.1 indicate that samples were collected from 391 participants for genotyping; 379 yielded successful sequences and 12 were unsuccessful. The count includes all individuals sampled for sequencing, not only successful sequences.",
      "answer": "391"
    },
    {
      "qid": 6,
      "question": "From which countries were the sequenced samples obtained?",
      "evidence": "\"The enrollment of participants was carried out in health facilities of eight regions of Cameroon: Centre, Littoral, East, West, Northwest, Southwest, North, and Far North.\" \"In each region, patients were recruited in both urban and rural sites at the hospitals with the highest patient frequency.\"",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "Section 2.1 locates all recruitment and sample collection sites in Cameroon; Table 1 on page 3 lists participating health facilities.",
      "answer": "Cameroon"
    },
    {
      "qid": 7,
      "question": "From what years were the sequenced samples obtained?",
      "evidence": "\"We carried out a cross-sectional and analytical study for five years, from December 2014 to June 2019.\" \"Patients presenting for ART initiation at the various recruitment sites were encountered by the recruitment clinician.\" \"For each participant, 10 mL of venous blood was collected in an EDTA tube.\"",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "Sections 2.1 and 2.3 describe sampling at enrollment during December 2014–June 2019.",
      "answer": "2014–2019"
    },
    {
      "qid": 8,
      "question": "Were samples cloned prior to sequencing?",
      "evidence": "\"Genotypic resistance testing was carried out in the pol gene (reverse transcriptase and protease regions) as follows.\" \"The predictive efficacies of each antiretroviral molecule were calculated according to the genotypic drug susceptibility score provided according to HIVdb algorithm (http://www.hivdb.stanford.edu, accessed on 24 May 2023).\"",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "Although patient samples were sequenced, no in vitro susceptibility data were reported. The specified applicability rule therefore requires Not applicable.",
      "answer": "Not applicable"
    },
    {
      "qid": 9,
      "question": "Which HIV genes were reported to have been sequenced?",
      "evidence": "\"Genotypic resistance testing was carried out in the pol gene (reverse transcriptase and protease regions) as follows.\" \"Regarding DTG efficacy, during the same study period, we reported a prevalence of 0% resistance to DTG in ART naïve patients, inferring 100% predictive efficacy of DTG [17].\"",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "Section 2.5 specifies PR and RT as the sequencing targets. Integrase resistance information was drawn from a separate cited study, not newly generated integrase sequences in this report.",
      "answer": "PR, RT"
    },
    {
      "qid": 10,
      "question": "What method was used for sequencing?",
      "evidence": "\"The products of the sequencing reaction obtained were purified by exclusion chromatography on SEPHADEX G50 resin and then sequenced using a genetic analyzer (ABI 3500®).\" \"Thus, the real prevalence of resistance would be better evaluated if we had a high-throughput sequencing technique (1% detection threshold), a platform unavailable in our context.\"",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "The ABI 3500 genetic analyzer specified in section 2.5 identifies capillary Sanger sequencing. The Discussion confirms that high-throughput sequencing was not available.",
      "answer": "Sanger sequencing"
    },
    {
      "qid": 11,
      "question": "What type of samples were sequenced?",
      "evidence": "\"For each participant, 10 mL of venous blood was collected in an EDTA tube.\" \"Viral RNA was extracted from 1 mL of plasma using the QIAGEN kit, following the manufacturer’s instructions.\"",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "Blood was collected and processed, but plasma was the specimen used for viral RNA extraction and sequencing in section 2.5.",
      "answer": "Plasma"
    },
    {
      "qid": 12,
      "question": "Were any sequences obtained from individuals with virological failure on a treatment regimen?",
      "evidence": "\"Included in our study were HIV-1 infected patients aged above 19 years (adults per WHO definitions) with no prior history of ART treatment.\" \"Not included in our study were patients who were re-initiating ART, those whose samples were unsuccessful at sequencing, and those who were co-infected with either viral hepatitis B or C.\"",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "Section 2.2 restricts the sequenced population to treatment-naïve adults and excludes ART re-initiators. No treatment-failure population was sequenced.",
      "answer": "No"
    },
    {
      "qid": 13,
      "question": "Were the patients in the study in a clinical trial?",
      "evidence": "\"We carried out a cross-sectional and analytical study for five years, from December 2014 to June 2019.\" \"The study participants consisted of adult patients initiating ART in the health facilities of regions previously cited.\"",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "Section 2.1 explicitly describes a cross-sectional observational study, not a treatment trial. The regimen comparisons were predictive analyses rather than randomized treatment assignments.",
      "answer": "No"
    },
    {
      "qid": 14,
      "question": "Does the paper report HIV sequences from individuals who had previously received ARV drugs?",
      "evidence": "\"Included in our study were HIV-1 infected patients aged above 19 years (adults per WHO definitions) with no prior history of ART treatment.\" \"Data collection was carried out using a pre-established data abstraction form at each site after obtaining a thorough medical history and clinical examination to minimize recruitment of participants with previous drug exposure.\"",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "Sections 2.2–2.3 describe treatment-naïve participants screened for previous drug exposure. No sequenced participant is reported to have previously received ARVs.",
      "answer": "No"
    },
    {
      "qid": 15,
      "question": "Which drug classes were received by individuals in the study before sample sequencing?",
      "evidence": "\"Included in our study were HIV-1 infected patients aged above 19 years (adults per WHO definitions) with no prior history of ART treatment.\" \"Not included in our study were patients who were re-initiating ART, those whose samples were unsuccessful at sequencing, and those who were co-infected with either viral hepatitis B or C.\"",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "The sequenced population was ART-naïve. Drug classes discussed for resistance interpretation or prospective regimen selection do not establish prior exposure.",
      "answer": "None"
    },
    {
      "qid": 16,
      "question": "Which drugs were received by individuals in the study before sample sequencing?",
      "evidence": "\"Included in our study were HIV-1 infected patients aged above 19 years (adults per WHO definitions) with no prior history of ART treatment.\" \"Data collection was carried out using a pre-established data abstraction form at each site after obtaining a thorough medical history and clinical examination to minimize recruitment of participants with previous drug exposure.\"",
      "evidence_location": "main_text",
      "rationale": "No previous ARV use was reported among the sequenced participants. Named drugs were discussed as resistance targets, candidate treatments, or background therapies rather than drugs received before sampling.",
      "answer": "None"
    }
  ]
}
